observations.text: Ladder in forecastle store did not have IMO symbols marking the escape route for use in darkness or blackout. Rectified during inspection by fitting IMO retroreflective tape on both sides of the ladder.

positives: Duty AB answered correctly that on an oil leak at the manifold he would inform CCR and press the emergency stop button, and showed the port and starboard manifold emergency stop locations
Bosun understood stop work authority when asked about the 3rd officer chipping without goggles
style: Ex-Chief Engineer, calm manner, asks questions but gives no personal remarks
Documents, SMS and PMS checked in the master's office only
Lifeboat, emergency generator, CO2 room, nitrogen room, paint locker, steering gear, workshop and engine room checked by visual inspection only, did not enter the lifeboat
Asks follow-up questions to test the depth of an answer, but does not record a failure as an observation if the person cannot answer

questions.q: If there is an oil leak at the manifold, what will you do?
What are the other locations of the emergency stops?
If you see the 3rd officer chipping without goggles, what will be your response?
If there is a blackout and the emergency lights are also not working, how will you escape from the forecastle store?
How much capacity does the emergency generator MDO tank have?
Will it be OK if the fuel is for 20 hours, or if the fuel is for 17 hours? Who decides this timing?
What is the SOLAS requirement for steering gear testing, in how much time, and who decides this? Why not 35-0-35 degrees or 30-0-35 degrees?

checks.item: SMS, PMS and documents checked in the master's office only
Lifeboat engine ahead and astern and rudder movement checked from outside, did not enter the lifeboat
Emergency generator visual inspection and QCV test
CO2 room and nitrogen room visual inspection
Steering gear, workshop and engine room visual inspection
15 PPM alarm and oily water separator operation tested in recirculation

tips: Make sure escape routes and ladders carry IMO symbols and retroreflective markings so they are visible in blackout conditions
Know all emergency stop locations on the manifold, not only the local ones
Be precise on minimum versus maximum fuel capacity for the emergency generator and who decides the timing
Be ready to explain the SOLAS steering gear test requirement of 35-0-30 degrees and the reason for the angles
summary: A calm ex-Chief Engineer inspected in Singapore, checking documents in the master's office and doing mostly visual inspection of the lifeboat, emergency generator, CO2 and nitrogen rooms, paint locker, steering gear, workshop and engine room. He asked practical questions to the duty AB, bosun and 4th engineer, and raised one observation about missing IMO escape symbols on the forecastle store ladder, which was rectified during the inspection. He cares about stop work authority, emergency stop locations and the reasoning behind SOLAS requirements.
